author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar said Saturday that his government will change a 2020 adoption rule that effectively barred gay and lesbian couples from adopting children. The announcement marks a significant policy reversal after Magyar defeated former Prime Minister Viktor Orban in April, ending Orban’s 16 years in power.

Before the 2020 law, one partner in a same-sex couple could apply to adopt as a single person. The Orban-era measure required single applicants to obtain approval from the family affairs minister, creating what Reuters described as an effective ban. Magyar said adoption decisions should be made by qualified professionals rather than a politician, though he did not provide a timetable or legislative text.

Hungary recognizes civil unions but does not allow same-sex marriage. The European Court of Justice ruled in April that separate Hungarian restrictions on LGBTQ content violated European law. Rewriting the adoption process would therefore become an early test of the new government’s approach to civil rights and its relationship with European institutions. The next concrete steps are the introduction of legislation and details about how professional adoption reviews would operate.
dek: Prime Minister Peter Magyar announced a reversal of the 2020 system but did not yet provide legislation or a timetable.
headline: Hungary moves to reverse restriction on gay adoption
